figmaExecutionNotes: Use a single design system token set across desktop and mobile; only change layout, spacing, and card density by breakpoint.
Keep hero as a standalone intro section and do not merge any form into it; no form content is provided in the source, so no form section is included.
Use the same feature card family across all feature sections to reduce component drift, while varying eyebrow labels and content density.
Do not invent missing pricing values; preserve pricing card structure with plan name, inclusion list, CTA, and trust line only.
Maintain enterprise trust hierarchy: hero first, trust bar second, then modular content blocks in a long-form sequence.
On mobile, collapse all multi-column grids into single-column stacks for readability and predictable Figma handoff.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a warm Zoho orange hero with a split layout: left-aligned copy and trust signal, right-side premium dashboard-style product composite. Keep the visual language operational and enterprise-ready, with white UI panels, soft shadows, and orange highlights. The hero should feel systemized and scalable, not editorial, with the product mockup showing unified email, chat, docs, meetings, and AI assistance.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a split, product-led dashboard composite to feel dynamic above the fold.
Trust is pulled immediately after hero as a compact credibility strip rather than buried later.
Product area alternates between a spotlight-plus-grid and a data-like insight band to avoid repeating the same card rhythm.
Testimonials use a carousel because there are 5 entries, breaking from the earlier feature-grid cadence.
Pricing is treated as a single highlighted conversion card to restore focus before the final CTA form.
No two consecutive sections share the same background; white and soft grey alternate, with a dark insight band for contrast.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email & Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Elevate team productivity with Zoho Workplace — a secure, enterprise-ready email and collaboration suite with real-time teamwork, AI productivity, app integrations, and 24x7 support.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand orange with layered floating dashboard chips and subtle gradient depth
sections.designNote: Make this a visual-first enterprise hero with the headline, supporting line, and compact benefit chips on the left; on the right, show a premium product dashboard mockup with email, chat, docs, meetings, and Zia AI cards. Keep the CTA strong and singular. This should feel energetic and confident, not minimal.
Place trust immediately after hero as a slim, high-clarity credibility band. Use the 100,000+ businesses proof as the primary message, with understated enterprise styling and minimal visual noise.

Use the first product block as the main explainer: a large spotlight card for the unified workspace, followed by a 3-column grid for collaboration, anywhere access, and AI productivity. The next product block should shift to a different visual cadence, using an accordion or split-panel list for growth, communication, integrations, and customization. Because the content volume is long and there are multiple product sections, alternate layouts within this area rather than repeating identical cards. This is the core modular storytelling section.

Keep this section concise and trust-supporting if included visually, even though the content payload is empty. Since there are no points provided, use this as a subtle credibility spacer or skip visible emphasis in implementation.

Make pricing a focused conversion moment with one centered enterprise card. Highlight migration assistance, storage, collaboration suite, and supported devices without overloading the section. This should feel clean, decisive, and action-oriented.

Use a carousel because there are 5 testimonials. Keep it visually lighter than the product and pricing blocks, but still polished. Include author, role, and company cues with a strong trust-forward tone.

End with a centered lead-capture card rather than a split layout, so the final action feels clean and low-friction. Reintroduce the 'Get Started' / free trial intent here, but keep the CTA rhythm controlled rather than aggressive.

blueprint.designPersonality: Efficient enterprise operations with a warm, confident brand voice; visually smart, systemized, and conversion-focused, with an orange-led dashboard aesthetic that feels modern and trustworthy.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium product composite: a laptop dashboard showing Zoho Mail, Cliq, Writer, and Meeting cards; overlay floating status chips like 'Secure Email', 'Live Collaboration', and 'AI Writing'. Support with subtle UI shadows, app tiles, and a clean enterprise workspace aesthetic. If real UI is unavailable, build a CSS-based mock dashboard with orange highlights and white panels.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline has 7 words, so a strong but slightly reduced 56px size keeps the split hero balanced and premium without wrapping awkwardly.

colours.colourReason: The brand’s primary orange (#ff6b00) must drive the hero background and primary CTA. White, black, and soft grey from the provided brand palette create a clean enterprise dashboard contrast. The accent deepens to near-black for structure and readability, while hover state uses a darker brand-safe orange derived from the primary.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo lockup, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and compact benefit bullets. Uses a strong top-intro area followed by a lead-capture form in the next block rather than a combined hero-form layout.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top hero/banner, then immediate form panel, then stacked content sections with repeating headline + description + feature list pattern. Rhythm is long-form and modular, prioritizing sequential information disclosure over dense multi-column storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content panels with minimal visual effects. Feature items are text-forward, lightly segmented, and likely bordered or spaced rather than heavily illustrated.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion action is presented in the hero as a single dominant CTA, with secondary conversion handled through a dedicated form section. CTAs are direct, utility-oriented, and repeated through the page rather than embedded in every section.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern is evident in the provided reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference structure.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible structure. Brand logo in the hero, with content driven primarily by typography and list-based benefits rather than large product imagery or video.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeating section template: small label/kicker, headline, short explanatory paragraph, then a feature grid or stacked feature list. Sections are grouped by theme and designed for scanning, with each feature represented by a title and concise description.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed immediately after the hero. Form is isolated in its own section to reduce distraction, using a strong heading and hidden metadata fields, implying a conversion-first lead capture flow.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit motion system is visible in the reference; if any motion exists, it is likely limited to standard page/UI transitions rather than narrative animation.
componentPatterns: Feature list/grid with title and supporting copy
designNotes: Conversion-first structure with a clear handoff from hero to form.
Typography-led layout with limited reliance on imagery.
Scannable long-form page architecture suitable for enterprise audiences.
Repeated modular sections support reuse across feature, integration, and benefit narratives.
Visual hierarchy is established through spacing and section sequencing more than decorative elements.

mustHaveMoments: Immediate enterprise value proposition in the hero with a clear Get Started CTA
Fast trust cue using the 100,000+ businesses social proof above the fold
Short benefit bullets highlighting unified workspace, collaboration, remote access, and AI productivity
A structured pricing/plan block with enterprise-ready inclusions and migration assistance
Multiple proof moments through testimonials and performance-stat feature cards
Clear trial-oriented CTA repetition through the page
avoidPatterns: Overly decorative or futuristic visuals that dilute enterprise credibility
Combined hero-plus-form layouts that clutter the first screen
Long introductory storytelling before showing product value
Heavy comparison framing since the intent is single-product conversion
Sparse sections that waste content depth or delay trust building
Generic stock imagery that does not communicate collaboration or business utility
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace is a single-product enterprise landing page with a long content map and strong existing proof points, so the page should focus on converting solution-aware buyers who are already evaluating collaboration suites. The structure should be product-led, with the hero immediately explaining the unified email and collaboration value, supported by stats-first trust messaging and repeated enterprise proof throughout the page. Because the goal is lead generation rather than pure awareness, CTA treatment should be strong and consistent, but the visual language should remain efficient and credible rather than flashy. A split hero is the best fit because it allows a clean headline-and-benefit presentation while preserving room for trust cues and a clear conversion path.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
